question: Which company built the spacecraft Michael Collins stayed in while the first Moon landing took place?
answer:
Michael Collins stayed in the command module Columbia, which was built by North American Aviation.

Collins was Apollo 11's command module pilot, and he stayed in lunar orbit aboard Columbia during the landing [[michael-collins]] "[stated] Stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia during the landing (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)".

Columbia was the Apollo 11 command module [[command-service-module]] "[stated] Apollo 11's command module was Columbia (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)". The command and service module was built by North American Aviation [[command-service-module]] "[stated] Built by North American Aviation (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)".

North American Aviation was the prime contractor for the Apollo command and service module [[north-american-aviation]] "[stated] Prime contractor for the Apollo command and service module (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)".

question: For about how long were the heaters of the tank that later exploded on Apollo 13 run on ground power before launch, and what did the investigating board say started the explosion?
answer:
Before launch, the tank's heaters were run on 65-volt ground power for about eight hours. [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Before launch it was emptied by running its heaters on 65-volt ground power for about eight hours (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)"

The Apollo 13 Review Board traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2. [[apollo-13-review-board]] "[stated] Traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2 (src: Apollo 13 Review Board report, 2026-10-24)"

The board's report called the switch failure a serious oversight in which all parties share. [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] "[stated] Called the switch failure a serious oversight in which all parties share (src: Michigan Daily 1970 coverage, 2026-10-24)"

The notes do not explicitly say the board named the thermostatic switches as the cause of the fire. The switch background is in the tank's facts: its heater specification was revised to 65 volts, but the switches were not changed. [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] The heater specification was revised in 1965 to 65 volts but the switches were not changed (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)"

Armstrong commanded Gemini 8, which was the first docking of two spacecraft in orbit, in 1966. My notes give only the year, not the exact date. [[neil-armstrong]] "[stated] Earlier commanded Gemini 8 in 1966, the first docking of two spacecraft in orbit (src: NASA biography, 2026-10-24)"

question: What was the improvised "mailbox" on Apollo 13 made from, and how did the crew build it?
answer:
The "mailbox" was an improvised lithium hydroxide CO2 scrubber adapter. Engineers devised it from hoses, cardboard, plastic bags and tape [[co2-scrubber-adapter]] "[stated] Engineers devised an adapter from hoses, cardboard, plastic bags and tape (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)".

It was needed because the command module's lithium hydroxide canisters were square and the lunar module's were round [[co2-scrubber-adapter]] "[stated] The command module's lithium hydroxide canisters were square and the lunar module's were round (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)".

The crew built it from radioed instructions [[co2-scrubber-adapter]] "[stated] The crew built it from radioed instructions (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)". The brain has no step-by-step construction details beyond that.

question: Put every 1970 date the brain records for Apollo 13 in order, with what happened on each.
